title: The RAM Warehouse
briefing: The RAM warehouse keeps stock in a dictionary: each RAM model is a key, and how many we have is its value. Today a delivery has arrived, we're adding a new model, retiring the old DDR3, and filling a customer order. Keep the books straight and Floor 1 is finished!
hints: Read or change a value with its key: inventory["DDR5"]. You can use += on it, and assigning to a new key adds it.
inventory.pop("DDR3") removes that key and gives back its value. order is a dict too, so order["model"] tells you WHICH model to take from. sum(inventory.values()) adds up all the stock.

inventory["DDR5"] += delivery, inventory["LPDDR5"] = 20, retired = inventory.pop("DDR3"), inventory[order["model"]] -= order["qty"], total_sticks = sum(inventory.values()), models = list(inventory.keys())
bonus: Use inventory.get("DDR9", 0) to look up a model that doesn't exist without crashing. Then try inventory["DDR9"] and read the error.
